title: Amelia Earhart's birth chart
metaDescription: Amelia Earhart's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 2.0° Leo. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Four of the ten placements whose signs are settled stand in Gemini — the Moon, Venus, Neptune and Pluto. The placements whose signs could change with an unknown hour are not counted. A cluster that size becomes the section the rest of the chart plays around.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: Measured rather than labelled, the Sun holds 2.0° Leo: the first decan, whose classical sub-ruler is the Sun. A fire sign, read here in its first face.

blocks.title: Closer to the ground
blocks.text: Day to day the chart speaks through Mercury in Leo (11.7°), Venus in Gemini (17.2°), Mars in Virgo (9.9°): a mind that decides at speaking speed, taste led by wit and proportion, drive that grinds rather than flares.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Closest first: Mars to Jupiter, a conjunction with 0.3° of slack. Two bodies in the same degree are not read as neighbours but as a merger: whatever one wants, the other is already funding. Behind it, Saturn conjunction Uranus at 0.9°, and Mercury sextile Pluto at 2.6° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. These are the day-proof angles — present at midnight, present at noon, present at the next midnight.

blocks.title: What the angles build
blocks.text: The Moon stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Of the seven planets the classical scheme judges, two sit in a sign it has an opinion about. The Sun in Leo at 2.0° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Jupiter in Virgo at 10.2° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain. The old table grades terrain, not talent — a placement in fall works uphill, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: The honest balance sheet uses the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: air 4, fire 2, earth 2, water 2 across the elements, and mutable 6, fixed 4 across the modalities. An air emphasis is read as distance for the sake of clarity: the idea gets examined before it gets adopted. Saturn and Uranus were retrograde — motion that reverses only from this vantage point, and which the old reading treats as delay used for revision.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Gemini for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 11.9° between midnight and midnight. The missing clock moves the Moon by half a sign at most here, and the boundary was never close. At the noon reference it stands at 6.2°.
